verdict.root_cause: platform-automation lowered ad's memory limit to 144m at 21:34:38Z, five minutes before onset, and unlike the eight prior lower/restore cycles this one was never reverted [tr_6ddf31bc8b26]. Under that limit the JVM cannot stay resident: ad shows four cold starts at ~60s intervals, each reaching AdService startup then dying with no shutdown line, no stack trace, no bind error and no in-process OutOfMemoryError — the signature of an external cgroup kill rather than an application fault [tr_03cb0064e103]. Each kill tears down the container, so frontend's gRPC client to 172.18.0.19:9555 fails at connect with EHOSTUNREACH / code 14 UNAVAILABLE against that single endpoint, with error timestamps advancing as retries keep failing [tr_54e3af93d73e]. frontend is the reporter, not the fault: its only changes are CART_ADDR churn already reverted to baseline an hour before onset [tr_80ad64f18b46]. The mechanism is memory exhaustion against a too-small limit; the edit is how it started.
verdict.reasoning: Three strands converge on ad: an unreverted memory-limit reduction active at onset [tr_6ddf31bc8b26]; a sustained ~60s crash/kill loop on ad with silent terminations, with graceful shutdown, JVM fatal error, bind conflict and startup failure all explicitly excluded [tr_03cb0064e103]; and frontend errors that are connect-level EHOSTUNREACH to one endpoint only, with deadline-exceeded, ECONNREFUSED, DNS failure, multi-dependency breakage and frontend-internal faults ruled out [tr_54e3af93d73e]. A container repeatedly destroyed and recreated makes its address unreachable exactly that way. frontend's change record offers no candidate [tr_80ad64f18b46]. Confidence is medium because both metric baselines returned HTTP 400 and measured nothing [tr_5867cb77b5bf, tr_ab9f73e6a1f0], so no memory-usage or restart series confirms the kill directly. Fix is restoring ad's baseline memory limit; a bare restart re-enters the loop.
open_questions: No direct OOMKill confirmation: container exit codes, kernel/orchestrator events and ad's working set versus the 144m limit were never retrieved; the kill mechanism is inferred from silent periodic termination.
The 172.18.0.19:9555 to ad mapping is conventional, not established by any retrieved evidence.
Six of eight services in blast radius were never dispatched and both Prometheus queries failed, so a broader shared cause with ad as one casualty is not excluded.

alternatives.root_cause: ad is killed every ~60s by a failing liveness probe or supervisor unrelated to memory, and the limit edit is coincidental automation noise.
alternatives.why_not: Does not explain why the single unreverted limit cycle is the one aligned with onset, and 144m is implausibly tight for a JVM with the OTel javaagent [tr_6ddf31bc8b26].

alternatives.root_cause: A host or network-level routing fault isolates ad's address from frontend while ad itself restarts for unrelated reasons.
alternatives.why_not: ad's own log shows no connectivity complaints during the incident minutes, only clean startups ending abruptly, and EHOSTUNREACH is fully explained by the container being repeatedly destroyed [tr_03cb0064e103].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring ad's prior resource configuration (removing the memory=144m limit applied at 21:34:38Z, the state the eight prior cycles reverted to) should let the JVM stay resident. Observable: in {service="ad"} logs, the ~60s cadence of cold starts (JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS pickup + OTel agent banner + 'AdService starting') stops — one startup banner after the recreate, then no further startup banners and continuous log output past the 60s mark and beyond. Downstream, {service="frontend"} should stop emitting new 'code: 14 UNAVAILABLE' lines with EHOSTUNREACH against 172.18.0.19:9555, with the embedded 'last error' timestamps ceasing to advance.
proposal.if_wrong: If ad logs a fresh cold-start banner ~60s after the recreate, the termination is not driven by the 144m cgroup limit — no OOMKill was ever confirmed (no exit codes, no kernel/orchestrator events, no working-set measurement; [tr_03cb0064e103] explicitly rules out any in-process OutOfMemoryError), so the mechanism is inferred from silent periodic death and could equally be a failing liveness probe or an external supervisor. Separately, if ad stabilises but frontend keeps logging EHOSTUNREACH against 172.18.0.19:9555, the IP:port-to-ad mapping is conventional only and the real unreachable endpoint is something else. A third falsifier: platform-automation re-applies memory=144m within minutes (it has done so eight times in this window), in which case the revert does not stick and the loop resumes — visible as a new resource_limits entry in change history.
proposal.risk: The container recreate kills the currently running ad instance: in-flight GetAds calls fail and ad's in-process cache is discarded, so the first post-revert requests are cold. If the diagnosis is wrong, we have added one more restart to a service already restarting, destroyed the live process state that would have supported the missing OOMKill confirmation (exit code of the dying container), and removed a memory ceiling that may have been deliberately bounding a genuinely leaking process — an unbounded ad could then pressure host memory and harm co-located services. The revert also fights an active automation loop; if that loop is the real defect, this is a cosmetic fix that masks it. Finally, six of eight blast-radius services were never dispatched and both Prometheus queries failed, so a broader shared cause with ad as one casualty is not excluded — this action would leave that cause untouched while appearing to resolve the incident.
proposal.blast_radius: ad only, for the duration of the recreate. frontend is ad's caller and is the reporting/alerted service; it sees the connect failure continue for a few extra seconds during recreate (it is already failing against this endpoint). frontend-proxy and the load path through it see the same, indirectly. No other service in the incident set (cart, checkout, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation) calls ad per the retrieved evidence, so they should see no change — if they do, that itself argues for the untested shared-cause hypothesis.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and its proxy firing simultaneously affect user-facing traffic and cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the simultaneous pair gives no clear fault signature yet.
